skill.name: dotnet-architect
skill.description: Expert .NET backend architect specializing in C#, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework, Dapper, and enterprise application patterns.
skill.summary: Guides .NET backend architecture, API design, data access, performance, testing, and deployment decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Complex .NET services need clear architecture, data access, and deployment choices. This skill guides API design, performance review, testing strategy, and enterprise patterns.
actual_capabilities: Designs ASP.NET Core APIs, services, middleware, and dependency injection structures.
Recommends data access patterns using Entity Framework Core, Dapper, repositories, CQRS, and transactions.
Reviews C# async, LINQ, memory, caching, and performance patterns for backend workloads.
Plans testing approaches with xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, WebApplicationFactory, and test containers.
Suggests deployment and observability patterns using Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, health checks, Serilog, and OpenTelemetry.
Explains architecture tradeoffs for Clean Architecture, DDD, vertical slices, microservices, and event sourcing basics.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not production validation in a live environment.
It cannot inspect private repositories unless the user provides relevant files or context.
It does not replace security, compliance, or performance testing for deployed systems.
Its recommendations depend on complete requirements, constraints, and success criteria.

use_cases.title: Plan a service architecture
use_cases.description: Create a clear service structure, data access strategy, and testing approach before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review performance risks
use_cases.description: Evaluate async usage, LINQ queries, caching, and database access for likely bottlenecks.

use_cases.title: Prepare deployment patterns
use_cases.description: Design health checks, containers, CI/CD flow, observability, and runtime configuration for .NET services.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Basic API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a small ASP.NET Core API for [domain]. Include endpoints, service boundaries, data models, validation, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Data Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Entity Framework Core and Dapper for [workload]. Recommend a data access pattern, transaction strategy, and query performance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .NET service design for maintainability, testability, security, performance, and deployment readiness. Identify risks and concrete improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize an Enterprise Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a phased modernization of [legacy .NET system]. Cover bounded contexts, API contracts, data migration, observability, rollout, and rollback strategy.

output_examples.input: Design a product catalog API with caching and database access.
output: Recommends service boundaries for catalog reads, writes, cache refresh, and inventory integration.
Suggests EF Core for transactional writes and Dapper for high-volume read projections.
Defines cache keys, invalidation rules, health checks, and integration test coverage.

output_examples.input: Review a LINQ query that causes slow page loads.
output_examples.output: The response identifies likely N+1 queries, unnecessary materialization, missing projections, and database indexing checks.

output_examples.input: Plan deployment checks for an ASP.NET Core service.
output: Defines readiness and liveness probes for the API and database.
Adds structured logging, tracing, metrics, and dashboard review steps.
Recommends staged rollout, rollback criteria, and smoke tests.

best_practices: Provide constraints such as scale, latency targets, database choice, hosting platform, and team experience.
Ask for tradeoffs, validation steps, and rollback options when making architecture decisions.
Share relevant code or diagrams when requesting reviews, and include known defects or performance symptoms.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad architecture recommendations without domain goals, constraints, or success criteria.
Do not apply every enterprise pattern when a simpler modular design solves the problem.
Do not accept generated code without tests, security review, and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Can this skill write C# code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft idiomatic C# examples, but you should test and review them before use.

faq.question: Does it support ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Minimal APIs, controllers, middleware, dependency injection, configuration, authentication, health checks, and rate limiting.

faq.question: Can it choose between EF Core and Dapper?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare both options for workload, performance, maintainability, transactions, and team skills.

faq.question: Will it deploy my application?
faq.answer: No. It can plan Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and observability steps, but it does not run deployments.

faq.question: Is it suitable for microservices design?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discuss service boundaries, API gateways, circuit breakers, observability, and distributed data concerns.

faq.question: Can it review existing architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide code, diagrams, requirements, or issue descriptions so it can identify risks and improvements.
